# Kvaesitso, patched for system navigation gestures

[Kvaesitso](https://github.com/MM2-0/Kvaesitso) built from its official release tag with a small set of
patches that make it behave better with Android's own navigation gestures. The result is signed with
one stable key and published as GitHub releases that [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium)
can install and update. Nothing here is a fork: this repository only holds the patches and the build
automation, and the source is fetched from upstream at a pinned release.

By hand: in Obtainium tap Add app, enter `https://github.com/cooligula/kvaesitso-gestures`, set the APK
filter to `\.apk$` (the checksum file is a second asset) and turn "Fallback to older releases" on.

## What is patched

| Patch | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`01-ignore-system-gesture-zone`](patches/01-ignore-system-gesture-zone.patch) | A touch that starts in the system gesture area (the home bar with gesture navigation) no longer moves the launcher's pages, and none of its swipe gestures fire from there. Android hands those touches to the system, but the launcher still sees them until the system takes over. That is the suspected cause of the launcher twitching, or opening the widgets or search page, around a swipe up to Home, to Recents or between apps ([#732](https://github.com/MM2-0/Kvaesitso/issues/732), [#1412](https://github.com/MM2-0/Kvaesitso/issues/1412), [#2038](https://github.com/MM2-0/Kvaesitso/issues/2038)). Nothing changes with 3-button navigation, where that area is empty. |
| [`02-home-press-only-for-home-intents`](patches/02-home-press-only-for-home-intents.patch) | The launcher runs its "home button" gesture action when it receives a new intent just after pausing. Now only a real Home intent (the home button or the home gesture) counts, not every intent that reaches the launcher, such as one from its own app icon or a shortcut. |

The patches work only inside Kvaesitso. Android's gesture navigation itself (the swipe animations and
Recents) is implemented by the system launcher, which is why a third-party launcher cannot replace it.

## Install and update

The application id is the one of upstream's release build, `de.mm20.launcher2.release`. This is a drop-in
replacement, with one catch: it is signed with a different key than the official APK or F-Droid, so
Android will not update one over the other. Make a backup in Kvaesitso's settings, uninstall the
original once, install this build and restore the backup. After that Obtainium updates it in place.

Versions look like `1.41.0-gestures.1`: the upstream version, and the revision of the patches on top of it.

## How releases happen

1. **Bump.** A daily workflow checks the latest full (non-pre-release) Kvaesitso release. When it is
   newer than the pin in [`upstream.toml`](upstream.toml), it opens a pull request that moves the pin and
   reports whether every patch still applies to the new version. If one does not, the pull request is a
   draft: rebase the patch on its branch.
2. **Verify.** The build workflow runs on that branch: it fetches the upstream tag, applies the patches
   and builds the app.
3. **Release.** Merging to `main` builds again, signs the APK with the release key and publishes a
   GitHub release. Merging a change to the patches alone publishes a new revision of the same upstream
   version. Merges that change nothing about the build publish nothing.

## One-time setup

The release job signs with the key you already use for your other apps. With the GitHub CLI logged in:

```sh
scripts/setup-signing.sh
```

It reads the key from `~/.losforgos-keystore` (never creates one), stores it as secrets in a `release`
environment that only the `main` branch can use, sets `CERT_SHA256` so any other key is refused, and
allows Actions to open pull requests. Then publish the first release:

```sh
gh workflow run build.yml --ref main -f release=true -f force=true
```

## Layout

- [`upstream.toml`](upstream.toml): the pinned upstream tag and commit, and the build settings.
- [`patches/`](patches/): the patches, in order.
- [`scripts/kvgestures.py`](scripts/kvgestures.py): bump, check, plan, fetch, prepare. Standard library only.
- [`.github/workflows/`](.github/workflows/): `bump.yml` and `build.yml`.
- `build-rev.txt`: raise it to force a rebuild of the current version without touching a patch.
